1720: The wheels touched the ground with a bump, a squeak, and a small round of applause you did not start.
1721: Baggage claim, where you and forty strangers stare at an empty belt and quietly root for the same corner.
1722: The belt started turning and every bag looked like yours for one hopeful second. None were. Then one was.
1723: First deep breath of a brand-new place. Smells like carpet, coffee, and possibility. Mostly carpet.
1724: You stepped into the terminal and the ceiling was so tall you forgot, briefly, why you came. Then remembered.
1725: A whole city out there, full of people, and not one of them is waiting to explain the streets to you.
1726: The tray table is stowed, the seat is upright, and your dignity is somewhere back around row twelve.
1727: You gave your neck a careful turn and it answered with a sound you'd rather not repeat. Onward anyway.
1728: Fresh page in the notebook, fresh city out the window, fresh pen that has decided, today, not to work.
1729: The captain thanked you for flying, as if you'd done the flying. You accept the credit anyway.
1730: You dusted yourself off, straightened your collar, and stepped out like someone who slept more than you did.
1731: A thief is out there settling in somewhere, cheerfully unaware that you just landed to ruin their week.
1732: Your coffee went cold somewhere over the water, but your curiosity did not. Priorities, correctly ordered.
1733: New streets you can't pronounce yet and don't have to. Your feet just need a direction, not a spelling.
1734: You walked through the arrivals doors and the day swallowed you whole, gently, like it does everyone.
1735: A brand-new place, and you get to be the one stranger in it who's actually looking for someone.
1736: Your suitcase wheels made a proud little clatter across the floor, announcing you to absolutely no one.
1737: The plane emptied one slow row at a time, and you counted every single one of them. Then you were free.
1738: You clutched a folded map you hadn't opened yet, saving all that confusion for a more convenient moment.
1739: Ground at last, holding so perfectly still that some restless part of you almost misses the swaying.
1740: A new city hums along without you, as it has for a few centuries and fully intends to keep on doing.
1741: You blinked into the bright terminal, found the nearest sign, and pretended it made total sense.
1742: You reached the overhead bin, retrieved your bag, and gently bonked no one on the way down. A quiet victory.
1743: You are here, freshly landed and slightly rumpled, ready to be useful the moment your knees agree.
1744: Ahead of you: clues, corners, and one very confident thief. Behind you: a left glove you won't see again.
1745: A new place stretches out in every direction, and every direction looks equally, thrillingly, unhelpful.
1746: You stepped off the plane a little wobbly, like a young colt, but with better shoes and a mystery to solve.
1747: A new stamp joined your passport, crowding in beside a dozen others like commuters at rush hour.
1748: Fresh start, fresh streets, fresh chance to ask three strangers the same question with growing hope.
1749: Your legs unfolded from the seat with the slow drama of something that had a very long day.
1750: The city doesn't know your name yet. Give it a few hours. Give it a case. It'll learn.
1751: You rolled to a stop at the curb and looked out at a place that owes you exactly nothing. Good. Fair.
1752: Off the plane, onto the moving walkway, gliding past everyone with the calm of a person who napped.
1753: New place, new air, new hum of a thousand people all being somewhere important without you.
1754: The bag came out last, of course, alone on the belt, doing one slow lap before you finally grabbed it.
1755: You stood at the edge of a place you'd never seen and thought, right, where does a person even begin.
1756: First step outside, and the whole busy world simply carried on, which is honestly the polite thing to do.
1757: You've landed, you've stretched, you've located a trash can and a sign. The investigation may commence.
1758: A brand-new terminal, humming and huge, and you the one small person in it who came here to work.
1759: The doors slid open with a friendly hiss and let you out into a place that was, until now, only a name.
